claim: A DNA damage-inducible mutagenic gene cassette has been implicated in the emergence of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis during anti-tuberculosis (TB) chemotherapy.
source: A DNA damage-inducible mutagenic gene cassette has been implicated in the emergence of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis during anti-tuberculosis (TB) chemotherapy.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior research cited in the manuscript and represents established knowledge in the field.

evidence: This is stated as the minimal composition based on prior work, though the full composition remains elusive.

claim: Following exposure of mycobacteria to DNA damaging agents, DnaE2 and ImuB co-localize with the DNA polymerase III β subunit (β clamp) in distinct intracellular foci.

evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Genetic inactivation of the mutasome in an imuBAAAAGG mutant containing a disrupted β clamp-binding motif abolishes ImuB–β clamp focus formation.
source: Notably, genetic inactivation of the mutasome in an imuBAAAAGG mutant containing a disrupted β clamp-binding motif abolishes ImuB–β clamp focus formation
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data showing absence of foci in the mutant strain.

claim: Griselimycin treatment of bacilli recapitulates the phenotype of abolished ImuB–β clamp focus formation observed in the imuBAAAAGG mutant.
source: a phenotype recapitulated pharmacologically by treating bacilli with griselimycin
evidence: This is supported by microscopy experiments showing loss of foci upon griselimycin treatment.

claim: Griselimycin collapses pre-formed ImuB–β clamp complexes in biochemical assays.
source: in biochemical assays in which this β clamp-binding antibiotic collapses pre-formed ImuB–β clamp complexes.
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography data showing disruption of the complex.

claim: The ImuB–β clamp interaction is essential for mutagenic DNA repair in mycobacteria.
source: These observations establish the essentiality of the ImuB–β clamp interaction for mutagenic DNA repair in mycobacteria
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of genetic and pharmacological disruption experiments.

claim: The mutasome represents a target for adjunctive therapeutics designed to protect anti-TB drugs against emerging resistance.

evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings.
